title: ChatticusBudgets construct with configurable limits
description:
**Phase 1 of 7.**

- **Blocked by:** nothing
- **Runs in parallel with:** the rest of phase 1
- **Unblocks:** the daily rollup

---
Supersedes the single-account shape of 79ca6a. A construct in infra/lib/ taking a monthly limit, alert thresholds, and notification targets, with defaults suiting a small deployment and a per-environment override. Every deployment gets one; none gets a hardcoded number.

**On the first limit:** the new account has no history, and that is a feature. Start low enough that any spend is signal, then raise deliberately. Spend from the previously shared account (161, 149, 190 dollars June to August) is not a baseline for a fresh account and must not be used as one.

**Runbook, not code:** cost allocation tags must be activated in the Billing console before any breakdown appears, and activation is not retroactive. A new account also reports nothing for roughly a day while Cost Explorer populates, which reads as a broken alarm unless it is written down.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
**#116 landed the first instance of this under 79ca6a. Generalize it; do not build a second one beside it.**

`ChatticusOrgSpendAlarm` already has the shape: account-level budget, thresholds at 50, 80, and 100 percent plus forecasted overage, SNS to an owner, and a deploy script that refuses to run without a monthly limit and a notification address.

What this card still adds is the part that makes it ship with every deployment rather than exist once here: limits and notification targets as construct props with defaults, so a new deployment gets budget tracking by standing the stacks up rather than by someone remembering to configure it.

Carry the refuses-invented-defaults behavior forward. A default limit is worse than no limit, because it looks like a decision.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
**Reviewed #125. The construct is right; its mounting point is not, and it carries a silent-deletion hazard.**

Good: reusable construct with props, conditional so CI without context synthesizes nothing, tests on both the TypeScript and Python sides, the refuses-invented-defaults behavior carried forward from 79ca6a, and the README documenting that a new account reports nothing for about a day while Cost Explorer populates.

**The hazard.** Budgets hang off `ChatticusSnapshots` behind `if (props?.budgetsConfig)`, and `deploy-chatticus-snapshots.sh` forwards `${BUDGETS_CDK_CONTEXT}`, which is empty when the environment variables are unset. Deploying the snapshot stack without them synthesizes a template with no budget, and CloudFormation deletes the budget and its SNS topic. That is the same class of failure this card avoided on the input side, arriving on the output side: a wrong limit is visible, a deleted budget looks exactly like a working one until the month it was needed.

Also worth weighing: AGENTS.md says never destroy `ChatticusSnapshots` because it holds the canonical snapshot store, and this makes it the stack you must redeploy to change a spend limit. Budget limits get tuned; snapshot buckets do not.

Carded as a follow-up rather than reopening this one, since the construct is sound and only its home needs to move.
